fact_1_ready_at_the_pin_on_the_real_remo.why: Ready at the pinned tag and commit, from the publisher's real remote

fact_2_tag_signature_verified_at_the_sou.why: the gitsign tag v1.1.0 was verified at the source boundary against nist's own pinned identity ^https://github\.com/policy-as-versioned-nist/nist/\.github/workflows/cut-release\.yml@refs/heads/(main|release/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.x)$

fact_3_last_applied_revision_equals_the_.why: nist is a verified source only (ticket 16 Q5): no Kustomization reconciles it, so the revision in force is the parent sha the composed set was built from. HEADER 33a05df1f524 vs pin 33a05df1f524. ONE LINK, NOT A SECOND PROOF: this reads composed/HEADER.yaml, the same composed set whose own fact 3 is the applied revision above -- the three fact-3 lines in this sample are one chain of custody, not three independent observations of a revision in force (ecosystem ticket 76)

fact_4_rendered_objects_byte_equal_to_an.ceiling: declared_equal, not byte identity: the API server defaults fields the render never declared. strict_equal is recorded per unequal object. A declared zero that the API server omits (an omitempty field of a built-in type, listed in render_composed.API_OMITTED_ZERO) reads as equal, and each object read that way is named under objects_read_through_omitted_zero (ticket 140).
fact_4_rendered_objects_byte_equal_to_an.why: all 17 rendered objects are live and equal to the offline render

fact_5_every_rendered_object_is_in_the_f.why: all 17 rendered objects appear in a Flux inventory

fact_6_the_bottom_rung_is_admitted_and_r.ceiling: the sidecar the cage injects at a hardened rung is a stand-in built from platform's own graded/waf-placeholder at the tag this repo pins. Running here means the caged workload started with the sidecar the cage added, not that a real WAF inspected anything.
fact_6_the_bottom_rung_is_admitted_and_r.why: the workload the cage put on its bottom rung (isolated) was ADMITTED and is Running, on priority class cage-isolated-5-0-0 (priority -10000), carrying 2 container(s) including waf-sidecar injected by the cage

fact_7_the_bottom_rung_reaches_nothing_w.ceiling: two pods in two namespaces, not one pod twice: in this cage the rung is a property of the NAMESPACE (ADR-0022) and never of the pod, so the control cannot be the same workload. Two TCP connects on two ports each -- the API server's ClusterIP and one address outside the cluster -- is not a proof that nothing at all is reachable. The control brackets the cage's reads rather than running simultaneously with them, so an outage entirely contained between two working control reads is still unobservable here; it is narrower than one read, not zero.
fact_7_the_bottom_rung_reaches_nothing_w.why: the cage in force put the fall-closed workload and the control on the SAME rung (isolated), so it has no bottom rung distinct from its loosest one and there was no bottom rung to look at

cluster_side_verification_passes_a_tag_t.why: nist's own release.yml is not in this checkout, so the identity it pins cannot be read here

verified_source_ready_but_the_object_is_.why: unhealed is a property of consecutive samples; `five-facts.py grade` fires this one by walking the log against the live intervals above
